questions.prompt: Find an equation of the plane with normal vector \((2,-1,3)\) passing through \((1,0,2)\).
questions.answer:
A plane with normal vector \(\mathbf n=(a,b,c)\) through \((x_0,y_0,z_0)\) has equation
\[
a(x-x_0)+b(y-y_0)+c(z-z_0)=0.
\]
Use \(\mathbf n=(2,-1,3)\) and \((x_0,y_0,z_0)=(1,0,2)\):
\[
2(x-1)-1(y-0)+3(z-2)=0.
\]
Expanding gives
\[
2x-y+3z-8=0.
\]
So one equation is \(2x-y+3z=8\).

questions.prompt: Decide whether the point \((2,-1,1)\) lies on the plane \(3x+y-2z=3\).
questions.answer:
Substitute \((x,y,z)=(2,-1,1)\) into the left side:
\[
3(2)+(-1)-2(1)=6-1-2=3.
\]
The result equals the right side \(3\), so the point lies on the plane.

questions.prompt: Find a normal vector to the plane \(4x-2y+z=7\).
questions.answer:
For a plane written as
\[
ax+by+cz=d,
\]
a normal vector is \((a,b,c)\). Here \(a=4\), \(b=-2\), and \(c=1\). Therefore a normal vector is
\[
(4,-2,1).
\]

questions.prompt: Find an equation of the plane through \((1,0,0)\), \((0,1,0)\), and \((0,0,1)\).
questions.answer:
Use two direction vectors in the plane. From \(P=(1,0,0)\), take
\[
\mathbf u=(0,1,0)-(1,0,0)=(-1,1,0),\qquad \mathbf v=(0,0,1)-(1,0,0)=(-1,0,1).
\]
A normal vector is \(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v\):
\[
(-1,1,0)\times(-1,0,1)=(1,1,1).
\]
Use the point \((1,0,0)\):
\[
1(x-1)+1(y-0)+1(z-0)=0.
\]
So
\[
x+y+z=1.
\]
